article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Triangle Kush × Z × Challah Bread
Breeder: DNA Genetics
THC Content: 24%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Diesel, sweet fruit, creamy pastry
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September into October
Indoor Yield: 425–540 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 14–19 oz. per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Zallah Bread is what happens when bright Z-style fruit collides with the darker side of Kush breeding. The first impression can be surprisingly sweet, with fruit and pastry-like notes rising above the flower, but the aroma quickly thickens into diesel, earth, pine, and penetrating gas. DNA Genetics created the cultivar by crossing TK Z with Challah Bread, bringing Triangle Kush and Z influence together with Bakers Delight and Kosher Kush ancestry. Instead of producing a simple dessert strain , the cross delivers a layered profile where confectionary sweetness repeatedly gives way to old-school fuel.

The plant follows the same theme of contrast. Zallah Bread is indica dominant, yet its early effects can feel mentally lively and creative before a much deeper physical calm develops. Dense resinous flowers, an 8–9-week bloom, and breeder-listed yields reaching approximately 19 ounces per square meter make it practical for production as well as connoisseur gardens. For cannabis growers who like modern fruit and dessert genetics but still want the weight, pungency, and resin of classic Kush marijuana , the cultivar brings those two styles together without allowing either one to disappear.
Genetics and Lineage

The official DNA Genetics pedigree is TK Z × Challah Bread. TK Z combines Triangle Kush with Z genetics, pairing a powerful Kush foundation with a sweeter fruit-driven side. Triangle Kush contributes much of the earthy, citrus, fuel, and physically relaxing character associated with the parent, along with dense resinous flower. Z shifts the aromatic direction toward fruit and candy, bringing brightness to a genetic foundation that would otherwise lean heavily into pungent Kush.

Challah Bread supplies the second parent and comes from Bakers Delight × Kosher Kush. Bakers Delight contributes the softer bakery side of the family, with sweet dessert aromas and Cookies- and Sorbet-related influence. Kosher Kush adds far more weight: earth, pine, pungency, heavy relaxation, and the strong OG family character that made it one of DNA Genetics’ best-known indica lines. Challah Bread itself was selected for combining bakery sweetness with an unmistakably Kush-dominant finish.

The completed cross therefore stacks multiple sources of gas and Kush beneath two different forms of sweetness. TK Z adds fruit and candy over a Triangle Kush base, while Challah Bread contributes pastry and dessert flavor supported by Kosher Kush. That arrangement explains why Zallah Bread can smell sweet at first but finish with considerably more diesel and earth than its name might suggest. It is a modern dessert hybrid built on a surprisingly traditional foundation.
Effects and Experience

Zallah Bread usually announces itself through the head before the body becomes fully involved. The first stage can feel euphoric, upbeat, and mentally engaging, with an increase in creative thinking and a lighter mood. Conversation may become more enjoyable, music more absorbing, and ordinary entertainment easier to become immersed in. DNA Genetics specifically describes the opening as cerebral and uplifting, which gives the cultivar more versatility than its indica-dominant classification alone would imply.

The character changes as the experience develops. Physical relaxation begins spreading through the body, gradually reducing the energetic quality of the opening and replacing it with a calmer, heavier state. Moderate servings can remain socially comfortable for some time, while larger amounts make the later Kush influence much more obvious. Muscles loosen, activity becomes less appealing, and the session can end in deep relaxation rather than sustained mental stimulation.

DNA Genetics does not publish one fixed THC figure for the seed line, so strength should be evaluated from the actual batch whenever laboratory testing is available. The breeder nevertheless describes the weed strain as potent and long lasting. Consumers with lower tolerance should avoid repeatedly dosing during the brighter early phase, since the later body effects can become considerably heavier than expected. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, or mental fog are possible after excessive consumption.
Medical Benefits

The transition from mental uplift into physical calm may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer a strain capable of serving more than one role during the same session. The early euphoric phase may help everyday stress, low mood, or mental fatigue feel less intrusive, while still leaving enough awareness for conversation or relaxed creative activity. That makes smaller servings potentially easier to use before the end of the day than marijuana that immediately becomes sedating.

As the Kush side becomes stronger, the body can feel substantially more relaxed. Muscular tightness and general discomfort may become less prominent, appetite can increase, and the experience may become more suitable for nighttime rest. DNA Genetics also emphasizes the cultivar’s deeply relaxing finish, but individual response still varies considerably. High-THC cannabis can increase anxiety in sensitive consumers, making gradual dosing more reliable than assuming indica-dominant genetics will always feel calming.

Because the breeder does not publish a standardized cannabinoid or terpene panel for every Zallah Bread phenotype, medical use should be guided by testing from the specific harvest when available. Different plants may emphasize sweet fruit, diesel, pine, or earthy Kush to different degrees, reflecting changes in aromatic chemistry as well as sensory expression. Personal tolerance, medications, dose, and previous response to cannabis remain more useful than broad strain claims.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Gas and diesel form the strongest foundation. Breaking apart a mature flower can release a sharp petroleum aroma accompanied by earth and Kush, creating a much heavier profile than the strain’s dessert-style name initially suggests. Pine may appear behind the fuel, adding a dry evergreen note that reinforces the Triangle Kush and Kosher Kush influence.

Sweetness enters from both sides of the pedigree but takes different forms. TK Z contributes fruit and candy, while Challah Bread brings a softer baked-goods quality. The combination can resemble sweet fruit layered over creamy pastry before the diesel returns through the background. Some phenotypes may push harder toward fruity Z characteristics, while others lean noticeably more toward earthy Kush and gas.

The flavor generally opens sweeter than the raw aroma. Fruit and creamy pastry can appear first, followed by earth, pine, and diesel during the exhale. Vaporization tends to preserve the lighter fruit and sweet compounds more clearly, whereas combustion makes the Kush and fuel substantially more dominant. A slow dry and careful cure help preserve the tension between sweetness and gas that gives Zallah Bread its identity.
Growing Information

DNA Genetics describes Zallah Bread as resilient and adaptable enough for both newer and experienced cultivators. Plants perform indoors and outdoors and respond well to basic canopy-management techniques. Topping and low-stress training can spread productive branches across the available light footprint, while selective pruning opens crowded interior growth and improves airflow. The breeder specifically recommends branch training to expose more flowering sites and increase usable production.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 8–9 weeks. DNA Genetics lists yields of 15–19 ounces per square meter, equivalent to roughly 425–540 g/m² under favorable conditions. Dense resinous flowers develop as bloom progresses, so late-flower humidity and air movement deserve close attention even though the cultivar is considered robust. A balanced nutrient program and consistent irrigation are preferable to aggressive feeding, and allowing the root zone to breathe between waterings helps avoid unnecessary stress.

Outdoor plants can produce roughly 14–19 ounces each, or approximately 400–540 grams under good conditions. DNA Genetics does not publish one fixed calendar harvest date because outdoor timing depends on latitude and the natural onset of flowering, but the same 8–9-week bloom generally places maturity from late September into October in many Northern Hemisphere gardens. Full sun, protection from extreme weather, and branch support near harvest can help the cultivar reach its production potential.
FAQ
What strains make Zallah Bread?
Zallah Bread was bred by DNA Genetics from TK Z × Challah Bread. TK Z combines Triangle Kush with Z genetics, while Challah Bread comes from Bakers Delight × Kosher Kush.
Is Zallah Bread indica or sativa?
DNA Genetics classifies Zallah Bread as an indica-dominant hybrid. The experience commonly begins with cerebral euphoria and creativity before becoming increasingly relaxing and body centered.
What does Zallah Bread taste like?
The flavor combines diesel and gas with sweet fruit, creamy pastry, earthy Kush, and pine. The inhale can lean sweeter, while the exhale often reveals more fuel and earth.
How long does Zallah Bread take to flower?

DNA Genetics lists an indoor flowering period of approximately 8–9 weeks. Outdoor maturity depends on local photoperiod and climate, generally arriving after the same eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle.
Is Zallah Bread a high-yielding strain?

Yes. DNA Genetics lists indoor production around 15–19 oz./m² and outdoor yields around 14–19 oz. per plant under favorable conditions. Training, light exposure, healthy roots, and environmental control all influence final harvest weight.
Final Thoughts on Zallah Bread

Zallah Bread works because its parents contribute different forms of intensity. TK Z supplies fruity sweetness over Triangle Kush fuel, while Challah Bread adds bakery notes backed by the deeper earth, pine, and relaxation of Kosher Kush. The finished cultivar therefore feels much more complex than a conventional dessert hybrid, moving repeatedly between candy, pastry, gas, and traditional Kush.

Its garden performance is equally practical. An 8–9-week flowering period, indoor yields of roughly 425–540 g/m², outdoor production around 400–540 grams per plant, and adaptable growth give cultivators a strong production framework without an unusually difficult routine. Basic topping, branch training, airflow, and consistent environmental control are generally more important than advanced cultivation techniques.

For consumers, the experience mirrors the pedigree. Cerebral euphoria and creativity define the opening, while deeper physical relaxation takes control later in the session. Combined with fruit, pastry, diesel, pine, and earth, that progression makes Zallah Bread a strong example of DNA Genetics blending contemporary sweet cannabis with the heavier Kush traditions that helped build its catalog.
